title: Classification of Living Things
description: Scientists sort living things into groups. All living things grow, need food, and reproduce. Animals are sorted by features like backbones, fur, feathers, or scales.

exercises.question: Which of these is a LIVING thing?
exercises.exp: A sunflower is alive — it grows, makes seeds, and needs water and sunlight.

exercises.question: Which is a NON-LIVING thing?
exercises.exp: A wooden table was once part of a living tree, but now it is not alive.

exercises.question: Which animal is a MAMMAL?
exercises.exp: Dogs are mammals — they have fur, are warm-blooded, and feed milk to their young.

exercises.question: Which animal is a BIRD?
exercises.exp: Penguins are birds — they have feathers, wings, and lay eggs. (Even though they can't fly!)

exercises.question: Which animal is a FISH?
exercises.exp: Salmon are fish — they have scales, gills, and live underwater.

exercises.question: Which animal is a REPTILE?
exercises.exp: Lizards are reptiles — they have scaly skin and are cold-blooded.

exercises.question: Which animal is an AMPHIBIAN?
exercises.exp: Frogs are amphibians — they can live in water AND on land, and have moist skin.

exercises.question: Which animals have a BACKBONE (vertebrates)?
exercises.exp: Fish, birds, and mammals all have backbones — they are vertebrates.

exercises.question: Which is an animal WITHOUT a backbone (invertebrate)?
exercises.exp: Butterflies are invertebrates — insects have no backbone, just a hard outer shell!

exercises.question: What do ALL living things need?
exercises.exp: All living things need food (energy), water, and some kind of shelter or habitat.

exercises.question: Which group has FEATHERS?
exercises.exp: Only birds have feathers — they help birds fly, stay warm, and stay dry.

exercises.question: A whale breathes AIR and feeds milk to its babies. It is a ___.
exercises.exp: Whales are mammals — even though they live in the ocean, they breathe air and nurse their young!

exercises.question: Which characteristic do ALL animals share?
choices: they all need food to survive and grow
exercises.exp: ALL animals need food for energy — whether they hunt, graze, or filter-feed. Food is essential for all animal life!

exercises.question: A SNAKE has scaly skin, lays eggs, and is cold-blooded. It is a ___.
exercises.exp: Snakes are reptiles — scaly skin, cold-blooded, and most lay eggs (though some give birth to live young).

exercises.question: Which animal has SCALES and GILLS?
exercises.exp: Trout (a type of fish) have scales to protect their body and gills to breathe underwater.

exercises.question: A FROG lives in water as a tadpole and on land as an adult. This makes it an ___.
exercises.exp: Amphibians live in both water and on land — frogs, salamanders, and toads are all amphibians.

exercises.question: Which group of animals NURSES (feeds milk to) their young?
exercises.exp: Mammals are the only animals that produce milk to nurse their young — from tiny mice to giant blue whales!

exercises.question: A MUSHROOM is ___.
choices: a plant — it is alive and grows in soil
a fungus — not a plant or animal
exercises.exp: Mushrooms are fungi — they are their own kingdom, separate from plants and animals. They decompose organic matter!

exercises.question: Which of these is NOT one of the five main groups of VERTEBRATES?
exercises.exp: Insects are invertebrates — they have no backbone. The five vertebrate groups are fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

exercises.question: What makes BIRDS different from ALL other animals?
exercises.exp: Only birds have feathers — that is the unique defining feature of birds. (Not all birds fly, but all have feathers!)

exercises.question: A SALAMANDER has moist skin and can live in water and on land. It is an ___.
exercises.exp: Salamanders are amphibians — moist skin, start life in water, and can live on land as adults.

exercises.question: Scientists group animals to ___.
choices: help understand how animals are similar and different, and study them better
exercises.exp: Classification helps scientists study, compare, and communicate about animals efficiently — it reveals evolutionary relationships too!

exercises.question: Which of these is an INVERTEBRATE (no backbone)?
exercises.exp: Snails are invertebrates — they have a soft body protected by a shell, but no backbone inside.

exercises.question: Both a BAT and a BIRD can fly. But a bat is a mammal, not a bird. What makes bats mammals?
choices: they have fur and nurse their young with milk
exercises.exp: Bats have fur (not feathers!) and nurse their pups with milk — two key mammal traits, even though they fly.

exercises.question: Which animal group has DRY, SCALY skin and is cold-blooded?
exercises.exp: Reptiles have dry, scaly skin and are ectothermic (cold-blooded) — they rely on the environment to regulate body temperature.

exercises.question: ALL living things can ___.
choices: grow, respond to their environment, and reproduce
make their own food from sunlight
exercises.exp: All living things share these traits: they grow, respond to their environment, reproduce, and need energy.

exercises.question: A STARFISH has no backbone. It is an ___.
exercises.exp: Starfish (sea stars) have no backbone — they are invertebrates with a unique water vascular system!

exercises.question: Which group has members that are BOTH aquatic (water) and terrestrial (land)?
exercises.exp: Amphibians divide their lives between water (as larvae/tadpoles) and land (as adults) — both environments!

exercises.question: A SPIDER has 8 legs and no backbone. It is an ___.
exercises.exp: Spiders are arachnids — a type of invertebrate with 8 legs. Insects have only 6 legs!

exercises.question: What do WARM-BLOODED animals have that cold-blooded animals do not?
choices: the ability to maintain a constant internal body temperature
exercises.exp: Warm-blooded animals (mammals and birds) regulate their own body temperature internally. Cold-blooded animals rely on the environment.

exercises.question: A PENGUIN has feathers but cannot fly. Is it still a bird?
choices: yes — having feathers is the key feature that makes it a bird
no — it is a mammal because it swims
no — it should be classified as a fish
exercises.exp: Yes! Penguins are absolutely birds — they have feathers, lay eggs, and are warm-blooded. Not all birds fly!

exercises.question: What does it mean to CLASSIFY living things?
choices: to give them all the same name
to group them based on shared characteristics
exercises.exp: Classification groups organisms by shared features — making it easier to study and understand the millions of species on Earth.

exercises.question: The largest classification group is called a ___.
exercises.exp: Kingdom is the largest group — all life is sorted into kingdoms (Animals, Plants, Fungi, Bacteria, Protists). Species is the smallest.

exercises.question: Fungi (like mushrooms) are in their OWN kingdom because ___.
choices: they are plants that moved underground
they are a type of animal
they are neither plant nor animal — they do not photosynthesize and absorb nutrients differently
they are a type of bacteria
exercises.exp: Fungi are unique — they are not plants (no chlorophyll, no photosynthesis) and not animals. They decompose matter and absorb nutrients!

exercises.question: Which feature is shared by ALL mammals?
choices: they all have fur or hair AND feed young with milk
exercises.exp: ALL mammals have fur or hair AND females nurse young with milk. This includes whales, bats, and even the platypus!

exercises.question: A whale lives in the ocean and has no legs. It is classified as a ___.
choices: mammal — it breathes air, is warm-blooded, and nurses young with milk
exercises.exp: Whales are mammals — they breathe air through blowholes, are warm-blooded, give birth to live young, and produce milk.

exercises.question: All living things are made of ___.
exercises.exp: All living things are made of cells — the basic unit of life. Some have one cell (bacteria), others have trillions (humans)!

exercises.question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of ALL living things?
exercises.exp: Not all living things walk — plants don't move from place to place. But all living things grow, respond, and reproduce.

exercises.question: A VIRUS is not considered a living thing because ___.
choices: it is too small to see
it cannot reproduce or carry out life processes on its own — it needs a host cell
exercises.exp: Viruses cannot reproduce or metabolize on their own — they must hijack a living cell. Scientists debate whether they are 'alive'!

exercises.question: What do REPTILES, BIRDS, and MOST FISH have in common?
choices: they all have scales or feathers (hard outer covering)
exercises.exp: Reptiles, birds, and most fish all lay eggs! Though eggs look different — fish eggs are tiny, bird eggs have hard shells.

exercises.question: A DICHOTOMOUS KEY helps scientists ___.
choices: measure the mass of an organism
identify an unknown organism by answering yes/no questions about its features
exercises.exp: A dichotomous key asks a series of yes/no questions about an organism's features to lead you to its correct identification!

exercises.question: Humans are classified as ___.
exercises.exp: Humans are mammals — we have hair, are warm-blooded, nurse young with milk, and give birth to live young.

exercises.question: Which of the following is an INVERTEBRATE?
exercises.exp: Jellyfish have no backbone (vertebral column) — they are invertebrates. Snakes, eagles, and frogs all have backbones.

exercises.question: Plants make their own food using sunlight. Animals cannot do this. This is why plants are ___.
exercises.exp: Plants are producers — they use photosynthesis to make their own food from sunlight, water, and CO₂. Animals must eat to get energy.

exercises.question: Which group of animals BREATHES THROUGH GILLS as adults?
exercises.exp: Adult fish breathe using gills — they extract dissolved oxygen from water. Amphibians use gills as tadpoles, then develop lungs.

exercises.question: An INSECT has ___ legs.
exercises.exp: All insects have 6 legs — no exceptions! Spiders have 8 (arachnids), and crabs have 10. Count the legs to identify an insect!

exercises.question: Bacteria are placed in their own kingdom because ___.
choices: they are too small to classify
they are prokaryotes — their cells have no nucleus, unlike all other kingdoms
they are plants that lost their chlorophyll
they are a type of fungus
exercises.exp: Bacteria are prokaryotes — their DNA floats freely with no nucleus. All other kingdoms (plants, animals, fungi) are eukaryotes with a nucleus.

exercises.question: The scientific name for a species uses two parts: genus and species. This system is called ___.
exercises.exp: Binomial nomenclature (two-name naming) was invented by Carl Linnaeus. Humans are Homo sapiens — genus Homo, species sapiens.

exercises.question: Which is an example of an ARTHROPOD?
exercises.exp: Spiders are arthropods — invertebrates with jointed legs and an exoskeleton. Insects, crabs, and centipedes are also arthropods!

exercises.question: What does BIODIVERSITY mean?
choices: the variety of different species in an area or on Earth
the number of plants in a forest
the average temperature of a region
exercises.exp: Biodiversity means the variety of life — the more different species in an area, the higher its biodiversity. It keeps ecosystems healthy!

exercises.question: A PROTIST is a living thing that ___.
choices: is a simple usually single-celled organism that does not fit neatly into other kingdoms
exercises.exp: Protists are mostly single-celled eukaryotes that don't quite fit as animals, plants, or fungi — like amoeba and algae!
